# Gate the orchestrate axis

Both answers changed the plan, so here is the whole thing again.

## packages/agents/skills/orchestrate/SKILL.md — the Skill states the contract

Attack it per /architecture: the consumer missed, the case narrowed, the capability dropped. Unchanged.

## packages/agents/agents/cto.md — one Principle

When orchestrating, the Architecture is the one thing only you hold. Unchanged.

## packages/agents/hooks/babysitter.py — the Stop call reads the turn's tool lines

You are right that the limited context breaks this as written. babysitter.py reads exactly two things: last_assistant_message off the event and the architect's last message through transcript.recent_user_texts. It never sees the turn's tool calls, and its own system prompt orders it to allow whenever a block would need context it was not given. So the call now carries transcript.current_turn_lines(transcript_path), which the rewake-side code already reads. Still one model call per Stop; the cost is prompt size.

## packages/agents/hooks/require_architecture_file.py — the gate reads the spine, not the disk

A plain existence check under docs/agents/ passes on any stale file from an earlier session, and those directories accumulate by design. The hook gets a PostToolUse half that stamps the written file's path into this session's spine through merge_state. The PreToolUse gate then checks that spine key. The spine is keyed by session id, so a parallel session's file can never satisfy the gate.

The allowance for each of these files is in docs/architecture/Architecture.md, which you asked about: a hook is per-turn Rules, and a Skill is one Process.
